mainTopic: Indirect damage by an animal (צרורות): whether we judge by the first action, and whether the half payment is collected from the animal's body or from the owner's best land.
overview: This amud deals with damage an animal causes indirectly, called צרורות. First the גמרא tests a ברייתא about chickens that pecked a bucket's rope until the bucket fell and broke. It asks whether this proves that we judge damage by the first action (בתר מעיקרא). It tries reading the ברייתא as the opinion of סומכוס, but the end of the ברייתא and רב אשי's open question rule that out. It then reads the ברייתא as the opinion of the רבנן. רב ביבי בר אביי pushes the proof away: the chicken's force carried the bucket the whole way. Next רבא asks a new question: is the half payment for צרורות collected only from the animal's body (מגופו), or from the owner's best land (מעלייה)? The גמרא tries to answer from a ברייתא about a hopping chicken and from a משנה about a dog that carried a loaf with a burning coal and set a stack of grain on fire. Each proof is challenged, and the reading that רבי אלעזר follows סומכוס and רבי יהודה is itself being questioned by רב סמא as the amud ends.

steps.title: The earlier dispute is really about pebbles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes rejecting an earlier proof: the תנאים there were not arguing about 'first action vs. final damage'. They were arguing about pebbles kicked up by an animal, which is the famous dispute of סומכוס and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case there is where the animal kicked up pebbles, and the תנאים are arguing about the same thing סומכוס and the רבנן argue about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing off an earlier attempted proof. It explains that the ברייתא's argument was about צרורות, not about רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this point, someone tried to use an argument between תנאים to answer רבא's question. The גמרא answers that the argument is simply the known dispute: the רבנן say pebble damage pays חצי נזק, and סומכוס says נזק שלם. So that source tells us nothing about 'first action vs. final damage'.

keyTerms.meaning: kicked up pebbles; damage an animal causes indirectly, by sending objects flying as it walks
the Sages; they hold that pebble damage is paid at half
they disagree

phrases.english: It is where it kicked up pebbles,
and they disagree about the dispute of Sumchus and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהִתִּיז צְרוֹרוֹת, וּבִפְלוּגְתָּא דְּסוֹמְכוֹס וְרַבָּנַן קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes an attempted proof begun before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The earlier attempted proof about following the first action
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute there is about צרורות (סומכוס vs. רבנן), not about first action vs. final damage.

steps.title: Proof from chickens that broke a bucket
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: chickens pecked at a bucket's rope, the rope snapped, and the bucket broke, and the owner pays full damage. The גמרא wants to conclude that we follow the first action.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: chickens were pecking at the rope of a bucket, the rope snapped, and the bucket broke. The owner pays full damage. Learn from this that we follow the first action!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to answer רבא's question. It suggests that we judge by the first action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chickens touched only the rope. The bucket broke afterward, when it fell. If we judged by the moment of breaking, the bucket would count as indirect damage, like צרורות, and would pay half. Since the ברייתא says full damage, it seems we judge by the first, direct act of the chickens.

keyTerms.meaning: pecking or scratching
full damages
we go after the beginning, judging by the first action

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Chickens that were pecking at the rope of a bucket,
and the rope snapped and the bucket broke –
they pay full damage.
Learn from this: we follow the beginning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier proof failed, a fresh proof is attempted.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's question: do we follow the first action or the final damage?
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of chickens, rope and bucket, which rules full damage

steps.title: The full payment is only for the rope
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof away: the 'full damage' in the ברייתא is for the rope, which the chickens damaged directly, not for the bucket.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain the ברייתא as talking about the rope.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chickens damaged the rope with their own bodies, so full damage for the rope is no surprise. The bucket may only pay half. If so, the ברייתא proves nothing about following the first action.

keyTerms.meaning: explain it, interpret it
rope

phrases.english: Explain it as referring to the rope.
phrases.notes: Meaning the full payment is for the rope. The bucket might only get half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion that we follow the first action
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The full payment may refer to the rope, not the bucket.

steps.title: But pecking at a rope is unusual
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: chickens don't normally eat rope. Unusual behavior falls under קרן and pays only half, so why full damage even for the rope?
steps.simpleTranslation: But a rope is unusual for them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Full damage for eating fits שן, where an animal eats what it normally eats. Chickens don't normally eat rope, so this is משונה. Unusual damage is treated like קרן and pays half, so the 'full damage' can't be for the rope.

keyTerms.meaning: unusual behavior for the animal, which falls under קרן and pays half
but surely; it opens a challenge

phrases.english: But a rope is unusual!
phrases.notes: He means it is unusual for a chicken to eat rope.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the full payment is for the rope
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating rope is unusual (משונה), so it should pay only half, not full.

steps.title: The rope had dough on it
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the rope was dirty with dough, so pecking at it is normal for chickens.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a rope dirty with dough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 3 by describing the rope differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rope had dough stuck to it, pecking at it is normal eating for a chicken. That makes it שן, which pays in full. So the rope reading still works.

keyTerms.meaning: dirty, soiled
kneaded dough

phrases.english: Where it was dirty with dough:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pecking at rope is unusual and pays half.
steps.terutzMaskana: A rope with dough on it is normal food for a chicken, so full damage applies.

steps.title: But it says the bucket broke
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: the ברייתא clearly mentions that the bucket broke, so the ruling must be about the bucket, not only the rope.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches that the bucket broke!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rope reading again, this time from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the ברייתא mention the bucket breaking if the payment were only for the rope? The wording shows the full payment covers the bucket too. So the rope answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: bucket
it teaches; the ברייתא states

phrases.english: But it teaches 'the bucket broke'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the attack on the rope reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the full payment is only for the rope
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly mentions the bucket, so its ruling covers the bucket.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: New answer: the ברייתא follows סומכוס, who holds that pebble damage pays in full. So even if the bucket counts as indirect damage, it still pays full.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is סומכוס, who says: for pebbles, one pays full damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the rope answer and gives a new way to reject the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Say we judge by the final break. The bucket would then be צרורות, indirect damage. According to סומכוס, צרורות pays in full anyway. So full payment for the bucket does not prove we follow the first action.

keyTerms.meaning: rather; it replaces an earlier answer

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא decided that we follow the first action. It is only saying the ברייתא could follow סומכוס, so the proof doesn't work either way.

phrases.english: Rather, it is Sumchus, who says:
Pebbles – one pays full damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rope answer after step 6 knocked it down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Full payment for the bucket shows we follow the first action.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to סומכוס, even indirect damage (צרורות) pays in full, so there is no proof.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא doesn't fit סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: Challenge from the end of the same ברייתא: a shard from the broken bucket broke another vessel, and the owner pays only half for that one. סומכוס never holds half damage for pebbles!
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is סומכוס, look at the end: a shard flew off the bucket, fell on another vessel, and broke it. For the first he pays full, and for the second he pays half. If it is סומכוס, does he hold of half damage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 7. The second half of the ברייתא seems to go against סומכוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second vessel was broken by a flying shard, which is clearly צרורות. The ברייתא says to pay half for it, which is the view of the רבנן. סומכוס would say full, so the ברייתא can't follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: say the end part; look at the latter clause
flew off, was sent flying
half damages
does he hold?; a rhetorical challenge

steps.whatToRemember: The bucket ברייתא was used to prove that we follow the first action. The גמרא pushed the proof away with סומכוס, but now the end of the ברייתא, which pays half for the second vessel, seems to rule out סומכוס.

phrases.english: If it is Sumchus, say the latter clause:
A shard flew off from it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the bucket the chickens broke.

phrases.english: and fell on another vessel and broke it –
for the first he pays full damage,
and for the last he pays half damage.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סוֹמְכוֹס, מִי אִית לֵיהּ חֲצִי נֶזֶק?
phrases.english: And if it is Sumchus, does he hold of half damage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the סומכוס answer of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows סומכוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the ברייתא pays half for the shard damage (צרורות), but סומכוס always pays full for צרורות.

steps.title: A possible defense: סומכוס treats a force of a force differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that סומכוס might pay full for a direct force (the bucket) but only half for a force of a force (the shard).
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that סומכוס makes a difference between damage done by the animal's force and damage done by the force of its force...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way to save the idea that the ברייתא follows סומכוס. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will knock this defense down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem from Step 8 was that the shard pays only half, while סומכוס says pebble damage pays full. The proposed fix is that the bucket is the chicken's own force (כחו), so it pays full, but the shard is a force of a force (כח כחו), and maybe for that even סומכוס gives only half.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a possible answer
Damage from the animal's force, like pebbles it kicks
The force of its force: a second-stage push, like the shard thrown by the broken bucket

phrases.english: And if you would say that for סומכוס there is a difference
between damage from its force and damage from the force of its force;
phrases.notes: The bucket is the chicken's force. The shard that flew off the bucket is the force of its force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A proposed answer to the challenge in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: direct force versus force of a force
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סומכוס pays full for every kind of indirect force, so the half payment for the shard contradicts him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe סומכוס pays full only for a first-stage force, and only half for a force of a force.

steps.title: רב אשי left this exact question unresolved
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asked whether סומכוס treats a force of a force like a force. If the ברייתא proved the answer, he would have used it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what about the question רב אשי asked: according to סומכוס, is a force of a force like a direct force or not? Let him answer it from this ברייתא: it is not like a force!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the defense from Step 9. רב אשי asked this very question and never answered it, so the ברייתא can't be the source of the distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא followed סומכוס and showed him paying only half for the shard, רב אשי's question would have an easy answer. Since רב אשי still treated it as an open question, we see that the ברייתא does not show סומכוס making this distinction. The idea that the ברייתא follows סומכוס is in trouble again.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked: raised an open question that needs an answer
Is like, is considered the same as
Let him resolve it: why not answer the question from this source?

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי's question is not attacking the ברייתא. The point is that his question is still open, which shows the ברייתא can't be read as answering it.

phrases.english: But then what about this question that רב אשי asked:
a force of its force, according to סומכוס,
is it like its force
or is it not like its force?
Let him answer it from here: it is not like its force!
phrases.notes: Meaning: if the ברייתא followed סומכוס, רב אשי could have answered his own question with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction proposed in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that סומכוס pays only half for a force of a force, as seen in this ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב אשי asked this exact question and left it open. If the ברייתא answered it, he would not have needed to ask.

steps.title: So the ברייתא must follow the רבנן, and we judge damage by where it started
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא follows the רבנן, then the bucket that broke somewhere else still pays full, which proves we go by the start of the damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't the ברייתא follow the רבנן? Learn from it that we go by the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: Since the ברייתא can't follow סומכוס, the גמרא suggests it follows the רבנן. It then draws a proof for the open question of בתר מעיקרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן pay only half for pebble damage. Even so, the ברייתא makes the chicken's owner pay full for the bucket, even though it broke when it landed. That only makes sense if we judge by the beginning, when the chicken first set the bucket in motion. Then the bucket counts as direct damage, and the shard, a later force, pays half like pebbles.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, who argue with סומכוס and hold that pebble damage pays half
Learn from it: we can prove something from this
We go by the beginning: we judge damage by the moment it was set in motion

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether we go by the start or the end of the damage was an open question earlier on the דף. This would settle it.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it the רבנן?
Learn from it that we go by the beginning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having ruled out סומכוס, the גמרא reads the ברייתא as the רבנן and draws a proof from it.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether damage is judged by where it started (בתר מעיקרא) or where it ended.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the chicken and the bucket, read as the רבנן: full payment for the bucket even though it broke on landing.

steps.title: No proof: the chicken's force carried the bucket the whole way
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי says the ברייתא is a case where the chicken's push kept moving the bucket all the way, so it proves nothing about going by the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: The case is where the bucket keeps going from the chicken's force, nonstop.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי בר אביי rejects the proof from Step 11. He explains the ברייתא as a special case that does not touch the open question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the chicken's own push kept the bucket moving until it broke, so the damage is fully the chicken's doing from start to finish. The open question is about a different case: an animal knocks a vessel, the vessel rolls away on its own, and then it breaks somewhere else. That question stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: Where it is going, still moving
From it, from it: driven nonstop by the original push

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא can't follow סומכוס, because רב אשי's question is still open. Reading it as the רבנן seemed to prove בתר מעיקרא, but רב ביבי בר אביי explains that the chicken's force moved the bucket the whole way. So the question of בתר מעיקרא stays unresolved.

phrases.english: רב ביבי בר אביי said:
Where it keeps going from it, from it.
phrases.notes: He means the chicken's push kept the bucket moving the whole time, with no break, until it broke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof for בתר מעיקרא. The reading that the ברייתא follows the רבנן can stand.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the bucket broke after the chicken's force had ended. In the ברייתא, the chicken's force carried it the whole way, so the case is not about the open question.

steps.title: רבא asks how half damage for pebbles is collected
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether חצי נזק צרורות is paid only from the animal's body (מגופו) or from the owner's best land (מעלייה). He gives a reason for each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: When an owner pays half damage for pebbles, does he pay only from the animal's body, or from his best land? Maybe from its body, because we never find half damage paid from the best land. Or maybe from the best land, because we never find damage done in the animal's normal way that is paid only from its body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question about how the half-payment for pebbles is collected. He gives a good reason for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two payment systems. A תם ox that gores pays חצי נזק, and only from the ox's own body. Normal damage, like walking (רגל), is paid in full from the owner's best property. צרורות are a mix of both: they come from normal walking, yet they pay only half. So which system do they follow?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked / raised a question (an open question, not an attack)
The half-payment for damage done by pebbles an animal kicks up while walking
From its body: payment is collected only from the animal itself
From the best-quality property of the owner
In its normal way of acting

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not asking HOW MUCH is paid. His question assumes the view of the רבנן, that it is half. He is asking WHERE the money comes from: only the animal's body, or the owner's general property.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the payment comes only from the animal's body, the owner never pays more than the animal is worth. If it comes from his best land, he can owe the full half-damage no matter what the animal is worth.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
The half damage for pebbles:
does he pay from its body,
phrases.notes: "Its body" means the animal itself. He can only collect up to the value of the animal.

phrases.english: or does he pay from the best land?
Does he pay from its body,
because we do not find half damage
that is paid from the best land,
or perhaps he pays from the best land,
because we do not find damage done in its normal way
that is paid from its body?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about צרורות, separate from the earlier discussion of a force of a force.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is חצי נזק צרורות collected only from the animal's body, like a תם goring, or from the owner's best property, like normal רגל damage?

steps.title: A teaching about a hopping chicken, read as pebbles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: for hopping, a chicken is not מועד, and some say it is מועד. Since hopping alone is obviously normal, the case must be hopping that sent pebbles flying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: For hopping, a chicken is not מועד. Some say it is מועד. Could it really mean plain hopping? That is obviously normal! Rather, doesn't it mean hopping that sent pebbles flying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer רבא's question. First it figures out what case the ברייתא is talking about. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hopping is just how a chicken walks, so of course it counts as normal behavior. It would make no sense to call it "not מועד." So the גמרא reads the case as hopping that kicked up pebbles, which is exactly the צרורות case of רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Hopping (a chicken's normal way of moving)
Considered a known, expected damager: pays in full from the owner's property
Would it enter your mind? (this cannot be the meaning)
Sent flying / scattered (pebbles)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For hopping, it is not considered forewarned.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is talking about a chicken.

phrases.english: And some say: it is forewarned.
Hopping, can that enter your mind?!
Rather, is it not hopping and sending pebbles flying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to answer רבא's question.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's question of whether צרורות pay from the body or from the best land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a chicken's hopping, read as hopping that kicked up pebbles.

steps.title: The two opinions match the two sides of רבא's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that "not מועד" means payment from the body, and "מועד" means payment from the best land. If so, רבא's question is an argument between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what they argue about: The one who says it is not מועד holds that he pays from its body. The one who says it is מועד holds that he pays from the best land?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It lines up the two opinions in the ברייתא with the two sides of רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumes the view of the רבנן, that pebbles pay only half. So "מועד" here can't mean full payment. It must mean collecting the half from the best land, like a מועד animal. "Not מועד" would mean collecting only from the animal's body, like a תם. So רבא's question would turn out to be an older argument.

keyTerms.meaning: They argue (about this point)
The one who says
He holds / is of the opinion

phrases.english: And in this they argue:
The one who says it is not forewarned
holds that he pays from its body,
and the one who says it is forewarned
holds that he pays from the best land?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 14 by explaining the dispute in the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Both sides of רבא's question have support among the תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two opinions in the chicken ברייתא (not מועד vs. מועד).

steps.title: No, they argue about the dispute of סומכוס and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא's argument may be the same as the argument between סומכוס and the רבנן, so it says nothing about where payment comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. They are arguing about the same thing סומכוס and the רבנן argue about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The ברייתא may be arguing about something else entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס holds that pebbles pay full damage, and the רבנן hold they pay half. So "מועד" in the ברייתא can mean "pays full," like סומכוס. "Not מועד" can mean "pays half," like the רבנן. Read that way, the ברייתא is about how much is paid, not where it comes from. רבא's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: No: the proof is rejected
A dispute / argument
סומכוס (pebbles pay full damage) and the רבנן (pebbles pay half)

steps.whatToRemember: The chicken ברייתא does not settle רבא's question. Its two opinions can be explained as the argument between סומכוס and the רבנן over full or half payment for pebbles.

phrases.english: No; in the dispute of Sumakhos and the Rabbis
phrases.notes: This is the argument mentioned earlier: סומכוס says pebbles pay full damage, the רבנן say half.

phrases.english: they argue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from steps 14–15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The ברייתא gives no information about רבא's question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed "מועד" must mean where the money comes from. It can instead mean full payment (סומכוס) versus half payment (רבנן).

steps.title: A dog takes a loaf and burns a stack of grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about a dog that took a loaf, ate it, and set a stack of grain on fire. The owner pays full damage for the loaf and half damage for the stack.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a dog took a loaf and went to a stack of grain. It ate the loaf and set the stack on fire. For the loaf the owner pays full damage, and for the stack he pays half damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try to answer רבא's question. This step only sets up the case; the proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating a loaf is normal for a dog, so that damage is paid in full. The fire, though, only gets half payment. The גמרא will ask why it is only half.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat loaf baked on hot coals
A stack of grain
Full payment for the damage

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A dog that took a loaf
and went to a stack of grain,
and ate the loaf and set the stack on fire:
phrases.notes: The fire came from a hot coal that was stuck to the loaf.

phrases.english: for the loaf he pays full damage,
and for the stack he pays half damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the ברייתא about the chicken was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source for רבא's question.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's question: is חצי נזק צרורות paid מגופו or מעלייה?
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about the dog, the loaf and the stack of grain

steps.title: Half for the stack is paid from the animal's body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the half payment is because the coal counts as צרורות. A ברייתא says this half is paid מגופו, so צרורות would be paid from the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason he pays only half for the stack? Isn't it because it counts as pebbles? And a ברייתא taught about this: he pays half damage, from the animal's body!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the proof. The fire counts as צרורות, and the ברייתא says the half is paid from the body, so that answers רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The coal fell off the loaf and lit the stack, just like a pebble that an animal kicks up. If this half is paid only מגופו, then חצי נזק צרורות is paid from the body.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Pebbles: damage done by something the animal sends flying
And a ברייתא taught about it
From its body: payment only from the value of the animal itself

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Is it not because it counts as pebbles?
And it was taught about it:
He pays half damage, from its body!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא – לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוְיָא לְהוּ צְרוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That חצי נזק צרורות is paid מגופו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on the משנה: 'he pays half damage, from its body'

steps.title: This reading does not fit רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. רבי אלעזר says the owner pays full damage for the stack. Do we ever find full damage paid only from the animal's body?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? According to רבי אלעזר, who says full damage, do we ever find full damage paid from the body?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof. If the ברייתא is read this way, it creates a problem for רבי אלעזר's opinion in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Payment only מגופו normally goes with half damage. רבי אלעזר says full damage here. If the ברייתא's 'from its body' fits his view too, then the case cannot be ordinary צרורות.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? A strong rejection
Do we ever find?

phrases.english: And can you really think so?!
According to רבי אלעזר,
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on, in words not quoted here, to say that רבי אלעזר holds he pays full damage for the stack.

phrases.english: full damage from its body: do we ever find that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of the ברייתא as being about צרורות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would mean that רבי אלעזר requires full damage paid only from the body, which is unheard of in plain צרורות.

steps.title: The dog acted unusually, so this is a case of קרן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the case as one where the dog acted unusually with the coal, which is קרן. רבי אלעזר follows רבי טרפון, who says unusual goring in the victim's yard pays full damage. So the ברייתא is not about צרורות at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where the dog acted unusually with this coal. And רבי אלעזר holds like רבי טרפון, who says: unusual goring in the damaged person's yard pays full damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the case that works for both opinions. This removes the proof for רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the dog acted unusually, the damage falls under קרן, not צרורות. Unusual damage is normally paid half and from the body. רבי אלעזר says full because of רבי טרפון's rule about the victim's yard, and the payment can still be from the body. So the ברייתא's 'from its body' teaches nothing about צרורות.

keyTerms.meaning: Acted unusually, not the way the animal normally behaves
A burning coal
Goring: the category for unusual damage
The yard of the person who was damaged

steps.whatToRemember: This answer explains the dog-and-loaf case as unusual behavior (קרן), which would remove the proof for רבא's question. The very next step (וְלָא הִיא) rejects this answer.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the stack damage is 'not damage' or that the owner is exempt. It is still damage he pays for; the case simply moves from צרורות to קרן.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case where it acted unusually with this coal,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן,
phrases.english: and רבי אלעזר holds like רבי טרפון,
who says:
Goring in the damaged person's yard is different:
phrases.notes: Usually unusual goring pays only half. רבי טרפון says that in the victim's own yard it is different.

phrases.english: he pays full damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty from step 19 by explaining the case in a new way, which also ends the proof from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case as קרן (unusual behavior) instead of צרורות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The half payment for the stack is because of צרורות, so the ברייתא proves that צרורות are paid מגופו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dog acted unusually, so it is קרן. רבי אלעזר follows רבי טרפון. The ברייתא says nothing about צרורות.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this answer stood, the משנה would teach nothing about צרורות. The next step challenges it, showing it was only needed because of the full-damage problem.

steps.title: Challenging the reading that follows רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the previous answer. The only reason to read the ברייתא like רבי טרפון was the full payment, and that problem can be solved another way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not right. Why did you set the ברייתא like רבי טרפון? Only because of the full damage payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the answer from step 20, which said the ברייתא is about קרן and follows רבי טרפון. It points out that the only reason for that answer was the problem of 'full damage.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the גמרא moved the case away from צרורות so that 'full damage from the body' could make sense under רבי טרפון. Here it says that move was only needed because of the full payment. If the full payment can be explained another way, the ברייתא can go back to being about צרורות. This step sets up the new explanation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so. A phrase used to reject an explanation just given.
You established it, meaning you explained the source as following a certain view or case.
Full damage, meaning payment of the entire loss.

phrases.english: But that is not so.
What is the reason you set it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא that says the owner pays from the animal's body.

phrases.english: in line with רבי טרפון?
Because of the full damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא; מַאי טַעְמָא מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20 by showing it depended only on the full-damage difficulty.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ברייתא as קרן following רבי טרפון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading was forced only by the full payment, which can be explained another way.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר holds like סומכוס and like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר may hold like סומכוס that צרורות pay full damage, and like רבי יהודה that the צד תמות stays. 'From the body' then refers only to the צד תמות half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר holds like סומכוס, who says צרורות pay full damage. He also holds like רבי יהודה, who says the צד תמות stays in place. So when the ברייתא says 'from its body,' it means the צד תמות part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to explain the ברייתא as a case of צרורות. The full payment comes from סומכוס, and the 'from its body' wording comes from רבי יהודה's idea of צד תמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that even a מועד keeps a 'תם side': half the payment comes from the animal's body like a תם, and the other half is paid like a מועד. רבי אלעזר applies this to צרורות, which pay full damage according to סומכוס. So half is paid from the body and the other half is not. The ברייתא's word 'מגופו' only describes that first half, so it no longer clashes with full damage.

keyTerms.meaning: Pebbles kicked up by an animal as it walks. Damage done indirectly in this way.
The 'תם side' of an animal: the half payment it would owe as a תם, which is paid from its body.
Stays in its place. The צד תמות is not erased when the animal becomes a מועד.
From its body, meaning payment comes only from the value of the damaging animal itself.

steps.confusionAlert: 'From its body' here does NOT mean the whole payment comes from the animal. Only the half that belongs to the צד תמות does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This brings back the reading that the case is צרורות. If it holds, the proof from step 18 returns: the first תנא's half payment for צרורות is paid מגופו. Step 23 now challenges this.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר holds like סומכוס,
who says: for pebbles
one pays full damage;
and he holds like רבי יהודה,
who says: the 'innocent side'
stays in its place.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה says this about an ox that became a מועד: it still pays half from its body, like a תם.

phrases.english: And when it teaches 'from its body,'
it refers to the innocent side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other way to solve the full-damage problem that step 21 hinted at.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difficulty from step 19: full damage paid only from the body.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining two views (סומכוס and רבי יהודה) to reread the word 'מגופו'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'From its body' covers the whole full payment, which is impossible, so the case cannot be צרורות.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'From its body' covers only the צד תמות half, so the case can be צרורות with full damage.

steps.title: רב סמא questions whether רבי יהודה's rule applies to צרורות
steps.stepSummary: רב סמא בריה דרב אשי begins to challenge רבינא. Maybe רבי יהודה only said צד תמות remains for an animal that started as a תם and became a מועד, and not for one that was a מועד from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סמא, son of רב אשי, said to רבינא: Say you heard רבי יהודה say this about a תם that became a מועד. But about something that is a מועד from the very start...
steps.whatsHappening: רב סמא starts a challenge to the explanation in step 22. He limits רבי יהודה's rule to an animal that changed from תם to מועד. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's idea makes sense when the animal really had a תם stage before becoming a מועד, as with קרן. צרורות are different: they belong to the category of walking (רגל), which is מועד from the beginning, so there was never a תם stage to 'remain.' If so, the explanation of step 22 may not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Say that you heard. This opens a challenge that limits how far a known opinion goes.
An animal that was innocent and became forewarned, like an ox that gored three times.
Forewarned from the start, like damage by walking (רגל), which animals always do.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: רב סמא, son of רב אשי, said to רבינא:
Say that you heard רבי יהודה say this
about an innocent animal that became forewarned;
but about one forewarned from its start...

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לְרָבִינָא: אֵימוֹר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of step 22 by limiting רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of רבי יהודה's צד תמות rule for צרורות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: צד תמות can only remain where there once was a תם stage. צרורות are מועד from the start, so there may be no צד תמות at all.
